content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data).**

What I found:
- **§ 13 (p0088)** gives Garman ownership of all IP in the Work *"including any Improvements or Modifications thereto."* "Modifications" is defined (§ 1(f)) as the changes set out in Schedule "D" — i.e. bespoke work we commission and pay for.
- Our counterbalancing rights come only from **§ 2 (p0028)**: a non-exclusive, non-transferable licence limited to Authorized Locations, with **§ 3** barring modification, sublicensing and transfer. That is short of the fallback's perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables.
- **No Customer Data ownership provision anywhere.** § 14 confidentiality protects data but does not allocate ownership, and § 4(b) (p0042) has Garman converting and handling Sparkling's data.
- Not walk-away: nothing assigns our IP or data to Garman, and Garman owning its platform and its Improvements is acceptable.

Redline (validated, `ok:true`) — one sentence inserted after § 13 confirming we retain all right, title and interest in Sparkling's data and materials with no assignment to Garman, plus a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use and modify the Schedule "D" Modifications and other deliverables built for us. § 17(a) already provides perpetuity while fees are paid, so no change was needed there.
